title: JS for ServiceNow: 1. Introduction
excerpt: Master JavaScript in ServiceNow from beginner to expert. Learn through real interview scenarios, step-by-step execution walkthroughs, and interactive examples.
content:
Welcome to Your JavaScript Journey

Whether you're an HR analyst automating leave calculations, an IT service desk manager building incident workflows, or a finance professional streamlining approvals—this tutorial series will transform you into a confident ServiceNow developer.

What makes this series different? We teach through the lens of real interview scenarios, show you exactly how code executes line by line, and give you working examples you can use immediately.

Why Server-Side First?

ServiceNow JavaScript differs fundamentally from web JavaScript. The platform's architecture demands a specific learning path. We start with GlideRecord because it's the gateway to everything else—once you master querying data, every other concept builds naturally.

💡 The Golden Rule: GlideRecord → Business Rules → Script Includes → GlideAjax. Never skip ahead. Each concept depends on the previous one.

The Learning Path

PhaseTopicsWhy This Order
Weeks 1-2JS Fundamentals + Platform BasicsFoundation for everything
Weeks 3-4GlideRecord + GlideSystem APIsCore database operations
Weeks 5-6Business Rules (before, after, async)Most important server script
Weeks 7-8Script Includes + Client ScriptsReusability + client-side intro
Weeks 9-10GlideAjax + UI PoliciesClient-server communication
Weeks 11-12Catalog Scripts + ACLsPortal and security

How Each Tutorial Works

Every lesson follows the PRIMM framework—a research-backed approach that dramatically improves retention:

1. Interview Scenario

🎯 SCENARIO: Your organization's Incident Management team reports that high-priority incidents assigned to inactive users remain unaddressed for days.

BUSINESS CONTEXT: User accounts become inactive when employees leave, but incidents may still reference them as assignees.

YOUR TASK: Write a Business Rule that automatically reassigns incidents from inactive users to the assignment group's manager.

2. Code Walkthrough with Labeled Steps

// === STEP 1: CHECK TRIGGER CONDITION ===
if (current.state == 6) {  // Resolved state
    
    // === STEP 2: VALIDATE REQUIRED DATA ===
    if (gs.nil(current.assignment_group)) {
        return;  // Can't proceed without group
    }
    
    // === STEP 3: PERFORM DATABASE LOOKUP ===
    var groupGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
    groupGr.get(current.assignment_group);
    
    // === STEP 4: UPDATE THE RECORD ===
    current.u_resolved_by_group = groupGr.getValue('name');
}

3. Execution Trace Table

LineActioncurrent.stateResult
1Check if state == 66true, continue
4Check if group is nil-false, continue
8Create GlideRecord-groupGr initialized
9Query for group-1 record found
12Set field value-"IT Support" assigned

For Non-Programmers: The Spreadsheet Bridge

Think of GlideRecord as a "database formula"—just like Excel formulas filter and transform data:

Excel ConceptServiceNow Equivalent
=SUMIF(range, criteria)GlideAggregate with addQuery
=VLOOKUP(value, table)gr.get(sys_id)
Filter by column valuegr.addQuery('field', 'value')
Sort A-Zgr.orderBy('field')
🚀 Pro Tip: Get a free Personal Developer Instance at developer.servicenow.com to follow along with hands-on practice.

Ready to start? Click Next to dive into GlideRecord fundamentals!

title: JS for ServiceNow: 2. GlideRecord Basics
excerpt: Master the most important API in ServiceNow. Learn to query, create, update, and delete records with real interview scenarios and execution traces.
content:
The Foundation of Everything

GlideRecord is the single most important skill for ServiceNow development. It's how you interact with the database—querying, creating, updating, and deleting records. Master this, and everything else becomes easier.

🎯 INTERVIEW SCENARIO: "Write a script that finds all active high-priority incidents assigned to the 'Network' group and updates their state to 'In Progress' if they've been open for more than 24 hours."

WHAT THEY'RE TESTING: Query construction, date comparisons, efficient updates, and understanding of when conditions.

Basic Query Pattern

Every GlideRecord interaction follows the same pattern: Create → Configure → Query → Iterate

// === CREATE: Initialize GlideRecord on a table ===
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');

// === CONFIGURE: Add your conditions ===
gr.addQuery('active', true);
gr.addQuery('priority', 1);  // High priority

// === QUERY: Execute the database query ===
gr.query();

// === ITERATE: Loop through results ===
while (gr.next()) {
    gs.info('Found: ' + gr.getValue('number'));
}

Execution Trace

StepWhat HappensDatabase Impact
new GlideRecord('incident')Creates object pointing to incident tableNone yet
addQuery('active', true)Adds WHERE active=true to internal queryNone yet
addQuery('priority', 1)Adds AND priority=1 to internal queryNone yet
query()Executes: SELECT * FROM incident WHERE active=true AND priority=1Database hit!
next()Moves pointer to first/next recordNone

The get() Shortcut

When you need exactly ONE record by sys_id or a unique field:

// By sys_id (most common)
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
if (gr.get('a1b2c3d4...')) {
    gs.info('Found: ' + gr.getValue('number'));
}

// By any unique field
var userGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
if (userGr.get('user_name', 'admin')) {
    gs.info('Admin sys_id: ' + userGr.getUniqueValue());
}
⚠️ ANTI-PATTERN #1: Null Variable Queries

When an undefined variable passes to addQuery(), ServiceNow returns ALL records where that field is NULL—potentially millions!
// ❌ DANGEROUS
var assignedTo;  // undefined!
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('assigned_to', assignedTo);
gr.query();  // Returns ALL incidents with no assignee!

// ✅ SAFE - always validate
if (assignedTo) {
    gr.addQuery('assigned_to', assignedTo);
}

Creating Records

var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.initialize();  // Prepares a new empty record
gr.setValue('short_description', 'Network outage in Building A');
gr.setValue('category', 'network');
gr.setValue('priority', 2);
var newSysId = gr.insert();  // Returns sys_id of new record

gs.info('Created incident: ' + newSysId);

Updating Records

var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('number', 'INC0010001');
gr.query();

if (gr.next()) {
    gr.setValue('state', 2);  // In Progress
    gr.setValue('assigned_to', gs.getUserID());
    gr.update();  // Saves changes
}
⚠️ ANTI-PATTERN #2: The GlideElement Pointer Problem

gr.field returns a GlideElement (pointer), not the actual value. This causes bugs when building arrays:
// ❌ WRONG - all items become the last record's sys_id
var ids = [];
while (gr.next()) {
    ids.push(gr.sys_id);  // Pushing a pointer!
}

// ✅ CORRECT - use getValue()
var ids = [];
while (gr.next()) {
    ids.push(gr.getValue('sys_id'));  // Pushing the actual value
}

Deleting Records

// Delete single record
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
if (gr.get('sys_id_here')) {
    gr.deleteRecord();
}

// Delete multiple records (use with caution!)
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('state', 7);  // Closed
gr.addQuery('sys_created_on', '<', gs.daysAgo(365));
gr.deleteMultiple();  // Deletes ALL matching records

Essential Query Operators

OperatorExampleMeaning
=addQuery('priority', 1)Equals
!=addQuery('state', '!=', 6)Not equals
>addQuery('priority', '>', 2)Greater than
INaddQuery('state', 'IN', '1,2,3')In list
CONTAINSaddQuery('short_description', 'CONTAINS', 'network')Contains text
ISEMPTYaddQuery('assigned_to', 'ISEMPTY', '')Field is empty

Performance: setLimit()

💡 Always use setLimit() when you only need a few records:
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('active', true);
gr.setLimit(10);  // Only fetch 10 records max
gr.query();
Without setLimit(), you might accidentally query millions of records!

Try It Yourself

🏋️ CHALLENGE: Write a script that:
1. Finds all incidents in "New" state (state=1)
2. That have been open for more than 48 hours
3. And have no assigned user
4. Update their priority to 2 (High)

Hint: Use gs.hoursAgo(48) for time comparison

title: JS for ServiceNow: 3. Business Rules
excerpt: Learn when and how to use Business Rules effectively. Understand before vs after rules, avoid common pitfalls, and master the 'current' and 'previous' objects.
content:
The Heart of Server-Side Logic

Business Rules are scripts that run when records are inserted, updated, deleted, or queried. They're the most powerful—and most commonly misused—server-side scripting tool in ServiceNow.

🎯 INTERVIEW SCENARIO: "An incident's priority should automatically escalate to P1 if it remains unassigned for more than 4 hours. How would you implement this?"

WHAT THEY'RE TESTING: Understanding of rule timing, when to use scheduled jobs vs business rules, and efficient database operations.

When Do Business Rules Run?

TypeWhen It RunsUse Case
BeforeBefore record is saved to databaseValidate data, set default values, modify current record
AfterAfter record is saved to databaseUpdate related records, send notifications, create tasks
AsyncAfter save, in backgroundHeavy processing, external API calls
DisplayWhen form loads (query)Set up client-side variables (g_scratchpad)

The 'current' and 'previous' Objects

// 'current' = the record being saved (with new values)
// 'previous' = the record before changes (read-only)

// Example: Detect if priority changed
if (current.priority.changesTo(1)) {
    gs.info('Priority escalated to P1!');
}

// Example: Detect any change to a field
if (current.state.changes()) {
    gs.info('State changed from ' + previous.state + ' to ' + current.state);
}

Execution Trace: Before Rule

Stepcurrent.stateprevious.stateDatabase
User clicks Save3 (new value)1 (old value)Still has 1
Before rule runs31Still has 1
Rule modifies currentModified1Still has 1
After rule completes--NOW saves current
⚠️ ANTI-PATTERN: update() in Before Rules

Never call current.update() in a Before rule! The system automatically saves current after the rule runs.
// ❌ WRONG - causes double save and recursion risk
(function executeRule(current, previous) {
    current.priority = 1;
    current.update();  // DON'T DO THIS!
})(current, previous);

// ✅ CORRECT - just set the value
(function executeRule(current, previous) {
    current.priority = 1;
    // No update() needed - system saves automatically
})(current, previous);

Before Rule Example: Auto-Set Assignment Group

🎯 SCENARIO: When a user selects a Category of "Network", automatically set the Assignment Group to "Network Support".
// Business Rule: Auto-assign Network Incidents
// Table: incident
// When: before insert, before update
// Condition: current.category.changesTo('network')

(function executeRule(current, previous) {
    
    // === STEP 1: Find the Network Support group ===
    var groupGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user_group');
    groupGr.addQuery('name', 'Network Support');
    groupGr.query();
    
    // === STEP 2: Set assignment group if found ===
    if (groupGr.next()) {
        current.assignment_group = groupGr.getUniqueValue();
    }
    
})(current, previous);

After Rule Example: Create Follow-up Task

🎯 SCENARIO: When an incident is resolved, automatically create a follow-up task for customer satisfaction survey.
// Business Rule: Create Survey Task on Resolution
// Table: incident
// When: after update
// Condition: current.state.changesTo(6)

(function executeRule(current, previous) {
    
    // === CREATE FOLLOW-UP TASK ===
    var task = new GlideRecord('task');
    task.initialize();
    task.short_description = 'Customer survey for ' + current.number;
    task.parent = current.getUniqueValue();
    task.assigned_to = current.assigned_to;
    task.description = 'Please contact customer to complete satisfaction survey.';
    task.insert();
    
    gs.info('Created follow-up task for ' + current.number);
    
})(current, previous);

Condition Field vs Script Conditions

ApproachWhen to Use
Condition field: current.priority == 1Simple field comparisons
Script: if (complexLogic()) {...}Multiple conditions, lookups, calculations
💡 Performance Tip: Put as much logic as possible in the Condition field. It's evaluated before the script even loads, saving processing time when conditions aren't met.

Controlling Execution Order

// Order field: Lower numbers run first (100, 200, 300...)
// Use 100-increment spacing for easy insertion later

Order 100: Validate required fields
Order 200: Set default values  
Order 300: Calculate derived fields
Order 400: Send notifications

Preventing Recursion

// Use current.setWorkflow(false) to prevent Business Rules 
// from triggering on your update

var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
if (gr.get(relatedIncidentId)) {
    gr.setWorkflow(false);  // Skip Business Rules
    gr.autoSysFields(false); // Don't update sys_updated_on/by
    gr.setValue('state', 6);
    gr.update();
}

Try It Yourself

🏋️ CHALLENGE: Create a Before Business Rule that:
1. Triggers when an incident's state changes to "Resolved" (6)
2. Checks if there's a resolution code
3. If no resolution code, sets one based on category
4. Logs the action using gs.info()

Hint: Use current.state.changesTo(6) in the condition

title: JS for ServiceNow: 4. Script Includes
excerpt: Build reusable code libraries with Script Includes. Learn the difference between classless and class-based includes, and when to use client-callable scripts.
content:
Write Once, Use Everywhere

Script Includes are reusable server-side code libraries. Instead of copying the same code into multiple Business Rules, you write it once in a Script Include and call it from anywhere.

🎯 INTERVIEW SCENARIO: "Your team has the same incident validation logic duplicated across 5 Business Rules. How would you refactor this?"

WHAT THEY'RE TESTING: Understanding of code reusability, Script Include patterns, and maintainability best practices.

Two Types of Script Includes

1. Classless (Simple Function Library)

// Script Include: IncidentUtils
// Client callable: false

function getIncidentCount(userId) {
    var count = 0;
    var gr = new GlideAggregate('incident');
    gr.addQuery('assigned_to', userId);
    gr.addQuery('active', true);
    gr.addAggregate('COUNT');
    gr.query();
    if (gr.next()) {
        count = parseInt(gr.getAggregate('COUNT'));
    }
    return count;
}

function isVIPUser(userId) {
    var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
    if (gr.get(userId)) {
        return gr.getValue('vip') == 'true';
    }
    return false;
}

Usage in Business Rule:

var count = getIncidentCount(current.caller_id);
if (count > 10 && isVIPUser(current.caller_id)) {
    current.priority = 1;
}

2. Class-Based (Object-Oriented)

// Script Include: IncidentHelper
// Client callable: false

var IncidentHelper = Class.create();
IncidentHelper.prototype = {
    
    initialize: function(incidentGr) {
        this.incident = incidentGr;
    },
    
    isHighPriority: function() {
        return this.incident.getValue('priority') <= 2;
    },
    
    getAssignmentGroupName: function() {
        var group = this.incident.assignment_group.getRefRecord();
        return group.getValue('name') || 'Unassigned';
    },
    
    escalate: function(reason) {
        this.incident.priority = 1;
        this.incident.work_notes = 'Escalated: ' + reason;
        return this.incident.update();
    },
    
    type: 'IncidentHelper'
};

Usage in Business Rule:

var helper = new IncidentHelper(current);

if (!helper.isHighPriority()) {
    var groupName = helper.getAssignmentGroupName();
    gs.info('Low priority incident for group: ' + groupName);
}

// Escalate if VIP caller
if (isVIPUser(current.caller_id)) {
    helper.escalate('VIP customer');
}

Execution Flow

StepWhat Happens
1. Business Rule startsScript loads
2. new IncidentHelper(current)Creates instance, runs initialize()
3. helper.isHighPriority()Calls method on the instance
4. this.incident.getValue()Accesses the GlideRecord passed in initialize

Client-Callable Script Includes

These can be called from client-side scripts via GlideAjax (covered in next chapter):

// Script Include: UserAjax
// Client callable: ✅ TRUE

var UserAjax = Class.create();
UserAjax.prototype = Object.extendsObject(AbstractAjaxProcessor, {
    
    getUserEmail: function() {
        var userId = this.getParameter('sysparm_user_id');
        var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        if (gr.get(userId)) {
            return gr.getValue('email');
        }
        return '';
    },
    
    isUserActive: function() {
        var userId = this.getParameter('sysparm_user_id');
        var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
        if (gr.get(userId)) {
            return gr.getValue('active');
        }
        return 'false';
    },
    
    type: 'UserAjax'
});
⚠️ Security Warning: Client-callable Script Includes are accessible from the browser. Never expose sensitive operations or bypass ACLs in these scripts!

Best Practices

💡 Naming Conventions:
  • *Utils - Utility functions (IncidentUtils, UserUtils)
  • *Helper - Class-based helpers (IncidentHelper)
  • *Ajax - Client-callable includes (UserAjax)
  • *Service - Integration/external service wrappers
// ✅ GOOD: Single responsibility
var IncidentValidator = Class.create();  // Only validation
var IncidentNotifier = Class.create();   // Only notifications

// ❌ BAD: God class that does everything
var IncidentDoEverything = Class.create();

Try It Yourself

🏋️ CHALLENGE: Create a class-based Script Include called "TaskHelper" that:
1. Accepts a task GlideRecord in initialize()
2. Has a method isOverdue() that returns true if past due date
3. Has a method getDaysSinceCreated() that returns the number
4. Has a method assignToMe() that sets assigned_to to current user

Hint: Use GlideDateTime for date calculations

title: JS for ServiceNow: 5. GlideAjax
excerpt: Connect client and server with GlideAjax. Learn asynchronous patterns, callback handling, and how to build responsive forms without page reloads.
content:
Client Meets Server

GlideAjax lets client-side scripts call server-side Script Includes without reloading the page. It's essential for dynamic forms, real-time validation, and fetching data based on user input.

🎯 INTERVIEW SCENARIO: "When a user selects a Configuration Item, you need to display its current status and owner from the server. How would you implement this without a page reload?"

WHAT THEY'RE TESTING: Understanding of client-server communication, asynchronous callbacks, and proper GlideAjax implementation.

The Two-Part Pattern

GlideAjax requires TWO pieces working together:

Part 1: Server-Side Script Include

// Script Include: CIInfoAjax
// Client callable: ✅ TRUE (REQUIRED!)

var CIInfoAjax = Class.create();
CIInfoAjax.prototype = Object.extendsObject(AbstractAjaxProcessor, {
    
    getCIDetails: function() {
        var ciId = this.getParameter('sysparm_ci_id');
        var result = {};
        
        var gr = new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci');
        if (gr.get(ciId)) {
            result.name = gr.getValue('name');
            result.status = gr.getDisplayValue('operational_status');
            result.owner = gr.getDisplayValue('owned_by');
            result.location = gr.getDisplayValue('location');
        }
        
        return JSON.stringify(result);
    },
    
    type: 'CIInfoAjax'
});

Part 2: Client-Side Script

// Client Script: Fetch CI Details
// Type: onChange
// Field: cmdb_ci

function onChange(control, oldValue, newValue, isLoading) {
    if (isLoading || newValue === '') {
        return;
    }
    
    // === STEP 1: Create GlideAjax instance ===
    var ga = new GlideAjax('CIInfoAjax');
    
    // === STEP 2: Set the method to call ===
    ga.addParam('sysparm_name', 'getCIDetails');
    
    // === STEP 3: Pass parameters ===
    ga.addParam('sysparm_ci_id', newValue);
    
    // === STEP 4: Execute with callback ===
    ga.getXMLAnswer(function(response) {
        var data = JSON.parse(response);
        g_form.setValue('u_ci_status', data.status);
        g_form.setValue('u_ci_owner', data.owner);
        g_form.addInfoMessage('CI: ' + data.name + ' at ' + data.location);
    });
}

Execution Flow

StepLocationWhat Happens
1BrowserUser selects a CI
2BrowseronChange fires, creates GlideAjax
3NetworkAJAX request sent to server
4ServerCIInfoAjax.getCIDetails() executes
5ServerGlideRecord queries database
6NetworkJSON response sent back
7BrowserCallback function runs with response
8BrowserForm fields updated, message shown
⚠️ ANTI-PATTERN: Synchronous GlideAjax

Never use getXMLWait() - it freezes the browser until the server responds!
// ❌ NEVER DO THIS - blocks the entire browser
var ga = new GlideAjax('MyAjax');
ga.addParam('sysparm_name', 'myMethod');
ga.getXMLWait();  // Browser freezes here!
var answer = ga.getAnswer();

// ✅ ALWAYS use async callback
ga.getXMLAnswer(function(answer) {
    // Handle response here
});

Error Handling

// Client-side with error handling
ga.getXMLAnswer(function(response) {
    try {
        if (!response || response === 'null') {
            g_form.addErrorMessage('Could not retrieve CI information');
            return;
        }
        var data = JSON.parse(response);
        // Process data...
    } catch (e) {
        g_form.addErrorMessage('Error processing response: ' + e.message);
    }
});
💡 isLoading Check: Always check isLoading in onChange scripts to prevent GlideAjax calls when the form first loads:
function onChange(control, oldValue, newValue, isLoading) {
    if (isLoading) return;  // Don't run on form load
    if (!newValue) return;  // Don't run if field cleared
    // ... rest of code
}

Try It Yourself

🏋️ CHALLENGE: Build a GlideAjax solution that:
1. Script Include "LocationAjax" with method "getLocationDetails"
2. Accepts a location sys_id parameter
3. Returns: building name, city, country, and manager name
4. Client Script that calls this when a Location field changes
5. Displays results in an info message

Hint: Don't forget Client callable = true!

title: JS for ServiceNow: 6. Advanced Patterns
excerpt: Master performance optimization, scoped applications, GlideQuery, and architectural patterns used by senior ServiceNow developers.
content:
Level Up Your ServiceNow Development

You've mastered the fundamentals. Now let's explore the patterns and techniques that separate senior developers from the rest—performance optimization, modern APIs, and architectural best practices.

🎯 INTERVIEW SCENARIO: "Your business rule is causing page load times of 15+ seconds. How would you diagnose and fix this?"

WHAT THEY'RE TESTING: Understanding of performance profiling, N+1 queries, batch operations, and optimization techniques.

The N+1 Query Problem

The most common performance killer in ServiceNow:

// ❌ N+1 PROBLEM: 1 query + N queries = slow!
var incGr = new GlideRecord('incident');
incGr.addQuery('active', true);
incGr.query();  // 1 query

while (incGr.next()) {
    // This runs a NEW query for EACH incident!
    var userGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
    userGr.get(incGr.assigned_to);  // N queries!
    gs.info(userGr.getValue('email'));
}
// Total: 1 + 1000 = 1001 queries for 1000 incidents!
// ✅ SOLUTION: Batch lookup with IN clause
var incGr = new GlideRecord('incident');
incGr.addQuery('active', true);
incGr.query();

// Collect all user IDs first
var userIds = [];
while (incGr.next()) {
    var userId = incGr.getValue('assigned_to');
    if (userId && userIds.indexOf(userId) === -1) {
        userIds.push(userId);
    }
}

// Single query for all users
var userMap = {};
var userGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
userGr.addQuery('sys_id', 'IN', userIds.join(','));
userGr.query();  // 1 query!
while (userGr.next()) {
    userMap[userGr.getUniqueValue()] = userGr.getValue('email');
}

// Total: 2 queries regardless of incident count!

GlideQuery: The Modern API

GlideQuery is a newer, more readable API for database operations:

// Traditional GlideRecord
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('active', true);
gr.addQuery('priority', '<=', 2);
gr.orderByDesc('sys_created_on');
gr.setLimit(10);
gr.query();
var results = [];
while (gr.next()) {
    results.push({
        number: gr.getValue('number'),
        short_description: gr.getValue('short_description')
    });
}

// GlideQuery equivalent - cleaner and chainable!
var results = new GlideQuery('incident')
    .where('active', true)
    .where('priority', '<=', 2)
    .orderByDesc('sys_created_on')
    .limit(10)
    .select('number', 'short_description')
    .toArray(10);

Efficient Record Updates

// ❌ SLOW: Update in loop
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('state', 1);
gr.query();
while (gr.next()) {
    gr.setValue('priority', 3);
    gr.update();  // Database write for EACH record!
}

// ✅ FAST: Use updateMultiple for bulk changes
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('state', 1);
gr.setValue('priority', 3);
gr.updateMultiple();  // Single operation!

// ⚠️ Note: updateMultiple skips Business Rules!
// Use setWorkflow(true) if you need them:
gr.setWorkflow(true);
gr.updateMultiple();

Recursive Protection Pattern

// Prevent infinite loops in Business Rules
var recursionCheck = 'BR_UpdateRelated_' + current.getUniqueValue();

if (gs.nil(gs.getSession().getClientData(recursionCheck))) {
    gs.getSession().putClientData(recursionCheck, 'true');
    
    try {
        var related = new GlideRecord('related_table');
        related.addQuery('parent', current.getUniqueValue());
        related.query();
        while (related.next()) {
            related.setValue('status', 'Updated');
            related.update();
        }
    } finally {
        gs.getSession().clearClientData(recursionCheck);
    }
}

Architecture Decision Guide

NeedUseAvoid
Simple field defaultBefore Business RuleClient Script (runs too late)
Update related recordsAfter Business RuleBefore Rule (current not saved yet)
Heavy processingAsync Business Rule / EventSync rules (blocks user)
Scheduled taskScheduled JobBusiness Rule with timer logic
Client-server dataGlideAjaxSynchronous API calls
Complex workflowFlow DesignerMultiple chained Business Rules
Reusable logicScript IncludeDuplicate code in rules

Congratulations! 🎉

You've completed the JavaScript for ServiceNow tutorial series! You now have the knowledge to:

  • Query and manipulate data with GlideRecord
  • Build server-side logic with Business Rules
  • Create reusable code with Script Includes
  • Connect client and server with GlideAjax
  • Optimize performance and avoid common pitfalls
🚀 Next Steps:
  • Build a complete scoped application
  • Explore Flow Designer for no-code automation
  • Learn IntegrationHub for external APIs
  • Study for ServiceNow certifications (CSA, CAD)

title: ServiceNow ITSM Automation: CMDB Best Practices and Workflow Optimization
excerpt: Discover essential best practices for automating ITSM in ServiceNow, focusing on maintaining an accurate CMDB for better decision-making and optimizing workflows with Flow Designer for efficiency.
content:
Introduction to ITSM Automation in ServiceNow

ServiceNow ITSM automation transforms IT service management by leveraging ITIL best practices, enabling organizations to streamline processes, reduce manual efforts, and enhance service delivery.

CMDB Best Practices for ITSM Excellence

title: Flow Designer Transaction Boundaries: What Every ServiceNow Developer Must Know
excerpt: Flow Designer executes asynchronously with no native rollback. Learn how transactions commit, when to use business rules instead, and proven compensating transaction patterns.
content:
Understanding Flow Designer's Execution Model

Flow Designer runs in the background with always a delay between trigger and execution start. Each database operation commits separately—there is no built-in transaction rollback across multiple actions.

Critical Design Decision

Use business rules when you need "ON BEFORE" execution or must run in the same thread as database operations.

Transaction Commit Timing

Each Flow Designer action that writes to the database commits independently.

// Flow execution timeline:
// Trigger: Incident created (committed)
// Action 1: Update CI (commits immediately)
// Action 2: Create Task (commits immediately)
// Action 3: REST call fails → Actions 1 & 2 already committed

When to Use Business Rules Instead

ScenarioUse Business RuleUse Flow Designer
Must run before DB write✓ Before BR✗
Same transaction required✓✗
Long-running process✗✓ Async
Multi-step orchestration✗✓

title: Scoped Application Security Patterns: Cross-Scope Access Done Right
excerpt: Navigate ServiceNow's scoped application security model with confidence. Learn cross-scope access patterns, ACL evaluation order, and security best practices.
content:
ACL Evaluation Order

ACLs evaluate from most specific to least specific:

  1. Field-level on specific table
  2. Table-level on specific table
  3. Field-level wildcard
  4. Table-level wildcard

GlideRecordSecure vs GlideRecord

// GlideRecordSecure automatically enforces ACLs
var grs = new GlideRecordSecure('incident');
grs.query();
while (grs.next()) {
  // Only returns records user can read
}

// GlideRecord requires manual checks
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.query();
while (gr.next()) {
  if (gr.canRead()) {
    // Safe to display
  }
}

Security Anti-Patterns to Avoid

  • Using gs.setSession() to bypass ACLs
  • Hardcoding admin credentials in integrations
  • Making all Script Includes client-callable
  • Storing sensitive data in client-accessible fields
  • Using eval() or dynamic script execution

title: Outage Prevention: Understanding Async Business Rule Risks and Scheduler Workers
excerpt: Prevent ServiceNow outages caused by async business rule backlogs, scheduler worker exhaustion, and recursive triggers. Learn monitoring and prevention patterns.
content:
Common Outage Causes

  • Recursive business rules: current.update() in After rules
  • Slow ACL execution: Complex scripts in ACL conditions
  • Long-running scheduled jobs: Consuming scheduler workers
  • Async business rule backlogs: Queue overwhelming workers

Scheduler Worker Exhaustion

ServiceNow has 8 scheduler workers by default. When all are consumed:

  • SLA updates block
  • Event processing stops
  • Emails queue indefinitely
  • Async business rules backlog
// Check scheduler worker status
var workers = new GlideRecord('sys_trigger');
workers.addQuery('state', 'executing');
workers.query();

gs.info('Currently executing scheduled jobs: ' + workers.getRowCount());

while (workers.next()) {
  gs.info('Job: ' + workers.name + 
    ' | Started: ' + workers.last_run);
}
